Libraries are often imagined as silent halls of dusty books, yet the modern public library is closer to a busy town square. People come to print job applications, attend coding workshops, borrow tablets, or simply sit in a cool room during a hot afternoon. For students who share a small home with a large family, the library may be the only quiet place to study. Critics argue that the internet has made libraries unnecessary, but this view overlooks a simple fact: access is not the same as ability. A free search engine is of little use to someone who cannot judge which sources are reliable. Librarians, trained to guide such searches, therefore remain as valuable as the books on their shelves.
